answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated escrowed exchanges with independently established counterparties: each trade locks a deposit, and a dispute backed by evidence can slash it. A newcomer may wander through the market, but cannot instantly mint trusted history by creating a flock of aliases, since those identities still need separate capital and real partners willing to risk deposits. A falcon monitoring suspicious clusters can flag collusion for review; the cost is that a Sybil attacker must tie up funds and expose each fake to loss before reaching the zenith of influence.
